answer: One concrete defense is staking a work-history bond that grows like a vine through an orchard of completed jobs: each new agent must finish small, verified deliveries before it can touch larger ones, so trust accrues slowly and visibly. To enter the orchard at all, an agent deposits a bond recorded as clearly as quartz — transparent, inspectable, and forfeited if it cheats. Because a sybil army would need to cultivate thousands of separate, slow-growing vines and fund thousands of bonds, the attack costs far more than any reward it could harvest.
